ACC Europe appoints Mark Maurice-Jones as president
stories.ltme_summary: The Association of Corporate Counsel Europe has appointed Mark Maurice-Jones as its president. stories.title: Express Solicitors appoints new chief executive
stories.ltme_summary: Express Solicitors Group has appointed Daniel Slade as chief executive, as the Manchester personal injury group reports revenues of £117.2m for the year to August 2026, up more than 34 per cent. The group has about 1,000 staff, has completed four acquisitions since its investment from Ufenau Capital Partners, and is investing in technology and AI. James Maxey stays on as Strategic Advisor.

stories.title: Former judge appointed terrorism legislation reviewer
stories.ltme_summary: Rupert Jones, a former judge, has been appointed Independent Reviewer of Terrorism Legislation and Independent Reviewer of State Threats Legislation, succeeding Jonathan Hall KC. He starts on 23 November 2026. The Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood praised his legal expertise. Jones will also carry out reviews for the Treasury and the Foreign Office under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018.
stories.hook: Former judge Rupert Jones takes over as terrorism legislation reviewer from 23 November

stories.title: University of California law school offers intensive course on AI legal tool building

Participants will work with Legora, Harvey and Replit to build legal AI tools. The course covers workflows, vendor evaluation and privilege and confidentiality in AI-augmented practice.

stories.title: Canadian Legal Summit 2026: is AI already your co-counsel?
stories.ltme_summary: The Canadian Legal Summit 2026 panel debated whether AI has become a practice partner. Microsoft's Jonathan Leibtag argued AI is already co-counsel, while Phil Brown of the Law Society of Ontario discussed professional responsibility and hallucination risk. Panellists agreed lawyers must define the value they add beyond what an algorithm can do.

stories.title: Mediation Fails to Resolve Fastcase-Alexi Lawsuit Over Alleged Data Misuse
stories.ltme_summary: A court-ordered mediation between Fastcase and Alexi did not settle their federal lawsuit, the parties told the court on 12 November. The dispute concerns a 2021 data licence and alleged misuse of Fastcase data by Alexi, a Toronto-based AI legal research company. Fastcase, now owned by Clio, sued in December 2025. The court has not yet responded to a request for a scheduling conference.
stories.hook: Fastcase and Alexi mediation fails, leaving Clio-owned Fastcase's data licence lawsuit unresolved

stories.ltme_summary: The American Arbitration Association has extended its AI Arbitrator, first used for construction cases, to documents-only business-to-business disputes across industries. The AAA says the tool drafts awards that human arbitrators must review and approve. It was trained on awards from more than 20 industries, according to the AAA.
stories.hook: AAA widens its AI Arbitrator to business-to-business disputes, with human arbitrators signing off awards

stories.title: Harvey puts access to justice on the agenda - with a little help from Amal Clooney
stories.ltme_summary: Harvey COO Katie Burke told Non-Billable the legal AI company expects to focus more on governments and courts in 2027. The comments follow a London event where Amal Clooney spoke on AI and access to justice. Harvey recently launched a UK, US and Australian pro bono programme with three firms, to build tools for high-volume legal work.

Founded in September 2025 by Will Rice, the London firm starts with UK residential conveyancing and says it reached $8 million annualised revenue within eight months. stories.title: Legal aid mileage gets 10p raise - but no backdate
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Aid Agency will raise legal aid mileage rates from 45p to 55p, matching HMRC, but will not backdate the change. The LAA says the rate applies from when the new regulations take effect.

stories.title: Legal services group's profits dip as law firms post modest growth
stories.ltme_summary: Ampa Holdings, a professional services group owning several law firms, reports revenue up 10 per cent to £142m for the year to 30 April, while profit before member pay fell 3 per cent to £29.9m. Designated member Keith Spedding says the group introduced Harvey AI across its legal teams. Debt drawn on a rolling facility reached about 95 per cent of its limit.
stories.hook: Ampa Holdings grows revenue 10 per cent to £142m but profit dips, with Harvey AI rolled out across legal teams

It cites ABA Formal Opinion 512 from July 2024 and says firms should first inventory AI use and check which vendor data terms apply. The author's views are opinion.
stories.hook: Lawyers pasting client data into chatbots raise confidentiality and privilege risks, commentary argues

stories.ltme_summary: The Patents Court has invalidated Boehringer Ingelheim's empagliflozin compound patent and its SPC for Jardiance, in a case brought by Dr Reddy's. The crystalline form patent was upheld as valid while in force.

stories.title: Pitilal v Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago: Privy Council upholds 2011 emergency but restores lawyer-access awards
stories.ltme_summary: The Privy Council has upheld the validity of Trinidad and Tobago's August 2011 state of emergency and its regulations, but restored compensation to two men denied access to a lawyer. The judgment is Pitilal v Attorney General [2026] UKPC 41, given by Lady Rose and Lord Doherty. The Board set a strict threshold for emergencies and found a breach of the right to legal advice.
stories.hook: Privy Council upholds 2011 Trinidad emergency but restores awards for denied legal advice

Almacantar v de Valk: Court of Appeal confirms cladding protection not limited to relevant defects
stories.ltme_summary: The Court of Appeal has held that the Building Safety Act 2022 cladding protection applies whether or not the defect is a relevant defect. Centre Point House leaseholders are therefore shielded from façade costs estimated above £12m.
entities: Almacantar Centre Point Nominee No.1 Ltd

stories.title: Southern Water v Environment Agency: tribunal nearly halves £1m Herne Bay sewage penalty
stories.ltme_summary: The First-tier Tribunal has cut Environment Agency variable monetary penalty against Southern Water over a 2024 Herne Bay sewage discharge from £1m to £525,000. The tribunal upheld culpability and harm findings but reworked the figure. It cited a one-quarter reduction for prompt self-reporting. The decision is Southern Water Services Limited v The Environment Agency [2026] UKFTT 1562 (GRC).
stories.hook: Tribunal halves Southern Water's £1m Herne Bay sewage penalty to £525,000

stories.title: Brown v Semelo-Shaw: joint tenants can claim rent repayment orders individually
stories.ltme_summary: The Upper Tribunal (Lands Chamber) has ruled that individual joint tenants can apply for rent repayment orders without their co-tenants. Judge Elizabeth Cooke allowed the appeal in Brown v Semelo-Shaw, with awards of £8,968.69 payable within 28 days.

stories.title: SKM v Essex County Council: school transport suitability extends beyond the journey
stories.ltme_summary: The High Court quashed Essex County Council's refusal to restore early drop-off and pick-up times for a 15-year-old with special educational needs. The judge held transport suitability must be assessed holistically, including access to education.

stories.title: Speech by the former Master of the Rolls: Mayflower Lecture
stories.ltme_summary: The former Master of the Rolls, Sir Geoffrey Vos, gave the Mayflower Lecture at the University of Plymouth on human rights and AI. He argues that economic pressure may push parties and governments toward AI-decided cases, and that it is hard to draw a clear line between cases suited to AI and those that need a human judge. The speech is dated 17 November 2026.
stories.hook: Former Master of the Rolls says economics may push courts towards AI decision-making

stories.ltme_summary: A study by HumanizeMy.ai, an AI writing and detection platform, found ChatGPT's link-tracking tag in 298 US federal court cases across 71 courts and in 133 SEC filings.
